takeaway: An RhD-negative mother exposed to RhD antigen at childbirth gets anti-D immunoglobulin, to reduce the risk of antibodies that would attack a later RhD-positive baby.

lines.text: This mother is blood group B, RhD-negative.
lines.say: This mother is blood group B, R h D negative.

lines.text: She has just given birth to a baby who is B, RhD-positive.
lines.say: She has just given birth to a baby who is B, R h D positive.

lines.text: Through childbirth, she has been exposed to the RhD antigen.
lines.say: Through childbirth, she has been exposed to the R h D antigen.

lines.text: Untreated, she would develop antibodies that would attack a later RhD-positive baby in the womb.
lines.say: Untreated, she would develop antibodies that would attack a later R h D positive baby in the womb.

lines.text: Anti-D immunoglobulin reduces her immune response, and so the risk of developing these antibodies.
lines.say: Anti D immunoglobulin reduces her immune response, and so the risk of developing these antibodies.

lines.text: Her haemoglobin of 11.0 needs no transfusion; that is usually considered below 8 g/dL.
lines.say: Her haemoglobin of eleven needs no transfusion; that is usually considered below eight grams per decilitre.

lines.text: So the correct pairing is this mother with anti-D immunoglobulin.
lines.say: So the correct pairing is this mother with anti D immunoglobulin.
